topology: CORE1 Gi0/24 ↔ SW1 Gi0/24 is the trusted root-facing trunk. SW1 Gi0/23 ↔ EDGE1 Gi0/24 is the designated protected boundary. PC1/PC2 use VLAN10 and 192.168.10.10/.20 on SW1/EDGE1 Gi0/1. PC3/PC4 use VLAN20 and 192.168.20.10/.20 on Gi0/2. Native VLAN99 and exactly allowed VLANs10,20,99 on both trunks; no router or host gateway.
verificationNotes: The ENCOR exercise shares the existing independent boundary-topology factory and retains the separate eight-task CCNA Root Guard entry. It adds fifteen tasks, a full three-switch configuration and two independently observed VLAN incidents. Practice starts at zero in PVST with all four trunk endpoints shut, all priorities32768 and no host PortFast. Four diagnostics remain enabled.

Published IOS commands configure Rapid PVST, base priorities CORE1 8192, SW1 16384, EDGE1 32768 for VLANs10,20,99, static matching trunks with DTP disabled, non-edge point-to-point switch links and four operational host edge ports. Only SW1 Gi0/23 has Root Guard; root-facing ports remain unguarded. BPDU Guard, Loop Guard and inter-switch PortFast are excluded from the intended boundary policy.

Configuration alone cannot establish a received trusted root or prove normal traffic. All three switches must elect CORE1 in every carried VLAN, with SW1 Gi0/24 and EDGE1 Gi0/24 Root FWD and SW1 Gi0/23 Desg FWD. Suppressing BPDUs prevents those goals; ordinary inferior BPDUs are accepted.

Lower only EDGE1 VLAN10 to priority4096, inspect actual received superior BPDUs and root-inconsistent blocking, and test all four PC directions. VLAN10 fails both ways while VLAN20 works. Repair only that priority to32768 and repeat the exercise independently in VLAN20, whose traffic now fails while VLAN10 works. SW1 and CORE1 retain the trusted root; EDGE1 may consider itself root inside the isolated VLAN. The physical trunk remains up and is not err-disabled.

Each incident task records actual root-inconsistent state on the enabled guarded port with received BPDU counters, using the existing bounded Root Guard lesson criterion. It does not require a fabricated event. Selective traffic results are validated during browser/test execution; incident credit itself is awarded for the observed protective state. The guide explicitly asks students to run all four diagnostics during each incident.

Both incident observations persist, while roots, roles, safe interfaces, correct priorities, saved policy and MAC learning are live. Final recovery requires both genuine incidents plus the fully restored healthy policy. Resetting an attacked port does not resolve the cause; removing Root Guard allows the rogue root and never counts as valid recovery. Simultaneous VLAN attacks remain independently blocked until each is repaired.

Normal traffic criteria correlate actual tagged request/reply identities and both bridge send/receive hops with preceding received version2 Rapid PVST BPDUs. Wrong packet parent IDs, tags or protocol versions cannot qualify. Normal traffic achievements remain historical after they are earned; diagnostics still show real failure during a later incident.

Eight live MAC checks cover all four access entries and all four remote hosts through SW1 Gi0/23 or EDGE1 Gi0/24. Clearing or expiry loses credit until new traffic relearns the entries. Saved/reopened labs retain fourteen achievements after BPDUs rebuild and require fresh traffic for the fifteenth MAC task. Renaming a device preserves stable-ID goals.

The existing shared rstp-saved projection now includes effective Root Guard, Loop Guard and BPDU Guard settings. Startup protection cannot differ from running protection while earning saved-policy credit. Tests toggle each saved flag independently and verify IOS reload restores an unsaved Root Guard removal. Full RSTP/MST/CCNA coverage remains in the regression suite.

The completed reference executes only published configuration commands, saves healthy startup policy and serializes empty runtime. It earns seven live configuration/tree/save tasks after new BPDUs converge, with no pre-earned incidents, packets or dynamic MACs. Students still perform both incidents and all traffic exercises.

Primary Cisco documentation informs designated-port protection, root-inconsistent rather than err-disabled state, per-VLAN containment and automatic recovery when superior advertisements cease. No new CML capture, CLI parser, forwarding algorithm, terminal styling, dependency or server backend is introduced.

Final Chrome file-origin QA covers light/dark at1440,390,320px: real IOS setup, both VLAN incidents and all four traffic directions during each, physical trunk and ROOT_Inc verification, priority-only recovery, fifteen tasks, clear/relearn, Windows pings, persisted reload, configuration-only reference and cancel/save-copy protection. Permalinks retain current host/path/query and select ENCOR Layer2 with five labs. CCNA Root Guard stays separate. Node/note fit, dialog fit and unchanged terminal golden styles are checked. Local preview returned HTTP200.
